title: Capacity-Agnostic Parameter Isolation for Continual Graph Learning
claim: Conventional parameter isolation propagates through the whole network; our decoupled subnetworks propagate only task-relevant, shared parameters, cutting computation as capacity grows.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, shared legend at left, zoomed weight matrices in center
description: A notation legend at far left defines four colors: orange for task t-1 neurons and parameters, blue for task t, green for shared or reused, and gray dotted for unused. Two timeline arrows (t-1 and t) head two neural-network diagrams. The left diagram is the conventional full-network propagation: one entangled layered network with both tasks' neurons and connections overlapping in a single blob. A dashed rounded box in the center zooms into color-coded weight matrices (w11, w12, and so on). Curved green and blue arrows show weights being reused or transferred. The right diagram shows decoupled propagation: separate orange and blue subnetworks, each with small weight blocks, linked by dotted lines to the matrices. The eye goes first to the colorful networks and the arrows.
caption: Intuitive comparison of full-network and decoupled propagation in parameter-isolation continual learning. Conventional
abstract: Existing parameter isolation-based continual learning methods employ diverse designs to accommodate more tasks within limited model capacity, but often incur increasing computational overhead as model capacity expands for growing task streams. To address this efficiency bottleneck, we propose CAGNN, a graph continual learning framework with a biological neuron-inspired architecture that features capacity-agnostic efficiency. CAGNN leverages graph contextual information to construct task-specific subnetworks and decouples them during training and inference, reducing full-network propagation overhead while enabling knowledge transfer across tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate CAGNN's superior effectiveness and computational efficiency over state-of-the-art methods.
